portInfo.description: APB places the modern port against Ibiza town’s nightlife and the medieval street maze of Dalt Vila. UNESCO’s World Heritage description (“Ibiza, Biodiversity and Culture”) ties the Renaissance walls (built 1554–1585 by Italian engineers Calvi and others) to later Phoenician–Punic archaeology at Sa Caleta and Puig des Molins, plus a marine Posidonia component. For a ship day, the cultural serial sites around Eivissa town matter more than the island’s club reputation.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Dalt Vila — Renaissance walls and Upper Town street fabric (UNESCO).
Puig des Molins necropolis / museum — Punic cemetery component of the WH property.
Harbour-edge town walk — APB’s own framing of port-beside-Dalt-Vila.
Punic necropolis of Puig des Molins
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Dalt Vila is steep. If mobility is limited, stay on lower harbour streets and the wall approaches that your energy allows rather than forcing the full circuit.
